reports.title: BellRing Brands Reports Results for the Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026; Provides Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook

guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook
section: •Fiscal year 2027 net sales and Adjusted EBITDA expected to range between $2.32-$2.42 billion and $310-$350 million, respectively

“Fourth quarter Premier Protein ready-to-drink consumption was our strongest of the year, and we were pleased to deliver consumption and sales growth ahead of our guidance with profitability in-line with expectations,” said Michael Axelrod, President and Chief Executive Officer of BellRing. “Fiscal 2027 will be a year of strengthening our foundation, sharpening our execution and driving cost savings to position BellRing for a return to sustainable, profitable growth. My first 100 days have reinforced my conviction in the significant opportunities ahead. We have strong brands, meaningful scale and a clear opportunity to drive more consistent performance and create long-term shareholder value. I look forward to sharing our refreshed strategy and long-term financial targets later this fiscal year.”

desk.headline: Sales up 7% to $692.0m, beat, but adjusted EPS falls to $0.22; FY27 outlook of $2.32–2.42bn sales
results: Net sales rose 6.8% to $692.0m as volume jumped 14.9%, but heavier promotions cut price/mix by 8.1%.
Adjusted gross margin fell to 20.1% from 29.7% on protein and tariff costs, freight, trade spend and $16m of inventory charges.
Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $66.4m from $117.4m; adjusted EPS fell to $0.22 from $0.51.
Full-year sales grew 3.5% to $2.40bn while adjusted EBITDA fell to $288.8m from $481.6m.
CFO Paul Rode steps down; Travis Leonard takes over on 1 Dec 2026.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: net sales of $2.32–2.42bn and adjusted EBITDA of $310–350m (about 14% of sales). The company also withdrew its long-term growth and margin targets pending a strategy review.

points: A low double-digit price rise on shakes took effect at the start of FY27; sales volumes are expected to dip in response.
High single-digit input cost inflation is expected, mainly from proteins, which are about 70% hedged.
A three-year supply chain programme targets at least $100m of gross savings, about $25m of it in FY27.
Competition in the club channel is expected to stay intense; non-club Premier consumption rose 17% in Q4.
Cutting net leverage from 3.6x to below 3x comes before buybacks; new long-term targets due with Q2 FY27 results.

watch: How much volume is lost after the shake price increase.
Gross margin recovery as savings and pricing meet protein cost inflation.
The refreshed strategy and long-term targets promised with Q2 FY27 results.
